answer: Prunings are heaped in the compost yard, and the yard keeper turns each heap weekly, recording the turning in the book. A karst heap claimed as turned fails the record: the heap must show the turning the keeper himself measured, and an unturned heap smells of rot. Faking a compost season takes a keeper, twelve weeks of false entries and 5,400 in wages, while the whisper entry in the yard book is checked at every planting, so a heap whose turning was never recorded is emptied by the estate, and the sparrow fork is kept in the keeper's hut as proof of the work.
